thread:
alex: Heads up — noticed a perf regression hitting hosted cluster this morning. p99 token latency for short-seq workloads (~<64) jumped across a bunch of routes.

alex: Quick repro notes below, but main hypothesis: kernel selector is preferring a fused/tiled path that has higher launch overhead; with continuous batching and lots of small requests the launch cost dominates.

alex: Profiling snippet from a problematic run (nsys + lightweight logs):
```
perf-summary:
p50  11.8ms
p95  33.6ms
p99  92.1ms  <- baseline last week ~48ms
trace-sample:
kernel_id: fused_attention_v2
kernel_launch_time_ms: 3.12
kernel_exec_time_ms: 0.42
batch_window_ms: 22
avg_seq_len: 28
requests_in_batch: 4
```

mei: :eyes: do you have a flamegraph or stack sample? launch_time looks suspiciously high for that kernel.

alex: I grabbed a couple stack dumps via perf/`perf record -g` and an nsys capture. flamegraph shows ~70% of wall time in CUDA kernel launch overhead and stream sync points for these short kernels.

samir: sounds like the selector cost model underweights launch overhead for small sequences. We optimize for pure kernel_exec_time which makes fused kernels look better, but they pay a launch penalty. With continuous batching (we're trying to keep latency SLOs) the batcher sends many small batches and kernel churn increases.

rachel: could KV cache behavior be amplifying this? if KV cold, seq_len effectively increases and we might flip kernels mid-session. Any correlation with cache miss rates?

alex: good point — I checked: sessions with hot KV have lower exec_time but still hit the same fused kernel. The issue occurs both hot+cold KV but is most visible when avg seq is <64 and batch size small.

oscar: two quick mitigation ideas: (A) tweak selector to add a launch_cost term into the scoring; (B) make sticky-kernel mapping sticky by seq-length bucket so we avoid churn across consecutive requests.

samir: prefer (A) + small canary. Example change: add launch_cost * alpha to score. Also we could add a heuristic: if seq_len < 64 prefer low-launch kernels even if exec_time a bit worse.

alex: toy patch I tested locally — small heuristic, improves p99 on microbench by ~20%:
```diff
diff --git a/runtime/kernel_selector.py b/runtime/kernel_selector.py
@@
-    if score_fused > score_tiled:
-        return 'fused'
+    # prefer kernels with lower launch overhead for short sequences
+    if seq_len < 64 and launch_cost > 1.0:
+        return 'small_launch'
+    if score_fused > score_tiled:
+        return 'fused'
```

rachel: can we add telemetry for kernel_launch_time_ms per kernel and handshake it with batcher telemetry (batch_size, batch_window_ms, seq_len)? we'll need that to prove regression root cause across customers.

oscar: yes — add metrics: kernel.launch_ms{kernel_id}, kernel.exec_ms{kernel_id}, batch.window_ms, batch.size, session.seq_len_bucket. Tag by model+variant+node.

perf-bot: scheduled: perf-cluster-phi job #482 queued (12h) — will run microbench + realistic traffic replay.

deploy-bot: canary deployed: kernel-selector tweak -> runtime-3 nodes on perf cluster. Rolling window 30m.

alex: next steps: (1) add telemetry (oscar), (2) run perf job + replay (perf-bot), (3) run canary 6h and gather p50/p95/p99 by seq bucket (samir + mei), (4) if positive, promote to canary on staging then production. I'll open an issue with logs and attach nsys captures.

mei: I can help triage the canary traces and produce flamegraphs.

samir: I'll prepare a revert-safe rollout plan and a small AB test weight change if needed.

alex: thanks all — created ticket RW-6284 with the plan and attached these snippets. Marking for follow-up in tomorrow eng-runtime sync. :thumbsup:
